column6: Back in stock at billboard scale; the shortage is the story and the three scents are the afterthought.
The same back-in-stock frame running three months; the urgency is permanent, which she will not check.
A starter pack plus smell incredible naked; the bundle removes the need to understand the range.
Answering a comment about which format is better; the shelf behind her is the evidence she has tried them all.
Underboob sweat printed as a headline; the OB/GYN line is what makes saying it out loud survivable.
What should you choose, then a quiz; the range has grown past the point where she can pick unaided.
The flavour drawn as a psychedelic landscape; the can is being sold as a graphic, not a drink.
Pure pattern with the can barely present; the art style is the brand recognition doing the work.
Cans on a picnic blanket; the can in hand is the point, and what it replaced is the unspoken half.
Grape rendered as a poster; she is picking a colour as much as a flavour.
Cans pegged to a washing line; the styling is doing the summer positioning the copy never states.
Cream soda given its own illustrated world; each flavour is treated as a separate product line.
The sound of water versus the sound of this; plain water is the incumbent being made to sound boring.
A face mid-reaction with no product in frame yet; the verdict arrives before the pitch does.
Can and poured glass side by side; the serve suggestion is what turns a flavour into an occasion.
Two men toasting cans at a theme park; the swap is being performed in the exact place a soda belongs.
Two cans clinked over grass; the gesture is a toast, which is the ritual being transferred.
A can styled with a coupe glass and jewellery; the staging says evening, and the drink says no alcohol.
Four women, four flavours, one grid; the range is being shown as a set of personalities.
